The proposed solution is incorrect. 

For an even-sized subset $T = \{t_1 < t_2 < \dots < t_{2k}\}$, the standard definition of the median is the arithmetic mean of the two middle elements, $M_T = \frac{t_k + t_{k+1}}{2}$. 

The proposed solution arbitrarily takes only the lower middle element $t_k$ as the median and completely omits the upper middle element $t_{k+1}$ (as well as the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$). As a result, the weights for $Q(A)$ are calculated incorrectly, breaking the inherent symmetry of the problem (evident even in the author's check for $n = 3$, where the true maximum difference is $P(A) - Q(A) = a_2 \le \max(A)$, giving $C = 1$, rather than $C = \binom{2}{1} = 2$).

VERDICT: REJECT
